solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Abandon heroin after police officer seizes it (5)

indicatorNotes.seizes: to seize is to grab and hold, so the officer's letters close round IT
indicatorNotes.after: after means following in order, so the heroin letter comes last

blocks.note: DC = Detective Constable, split around IT
H is slang shorthand for heroin

annotation.surface: A drug raid in which a policeman grabs the heroin and gives up on it.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug-squad picture points at a busted dealer; the definition is the plain verb at the front, meaning to dump something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to get rid of or leave behind, as a car dumped in a river or a plan dropped halfway.

entries.clue: Needing lies to be circulated, European that has a thirst for power? (6,6)

annotation.definition: that has a thirst for power?
annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the thing that has the thirst: the engine

indicatorNotes.to be circulated: something circulated is passed round and round, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: E = European, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A European who needs rumours spread in order to feed an appetite for power.
annotation.walkthrough: The power-hungry European is a political picture; the question mark signals that the thirst is for fuel, and the power is horsepower.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: this machine drinks fuel in order to deliver mechanical power, so its 'thirst' is literal.

entries.clue: It’s in the tenth part (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says one thing is located inside another, so IT is placed within THE

blocks.note: used as printed, split around IT

annotation.surface: A plain statement that something lies in the tenth part.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is almost entirely wordplay read literally: IT is in THE. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal meaning: a tenth of produce or income, traditionally paid to support the church.

entries.clue: Suspended over answer, managed to bite one’s tongue (9)

indicatorNotes.over: over means on top of, and in a down clue the first piece sits above the rest
indicatorNotes.to bite: biting closes the teeth round something, so RAN closes round I

blocks.note: ran = managed, as a business; split around I

annotation.surface: Someone left hanging over a reply who manages to hold their tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bite one's tongue' reads as an idiom for staying silent; here 'bite one' is the container and 'tongue' alone is the definition, a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Tongue in its sense of a language; this is the language of Hungary, also called Magyar.

entries.clue: Rat’s expression of disdain when eating rotten acorn (8)

indicatorNotes.when eating: eating takes something inside, so TUT swallows the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.rotten: a rotten thing has decayed out of its proper form, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: tut! expresses disapproval; split around the anagram

annotation.surface: A rat sniffing disdainfully as it munches a rotten acorn.
annotation.walkthrough: The animal picture hides the other sense of rat: a traitor.
annotation.definitionFit: Rat as a noun for a deserter or betrayer, someone who switches sides, as one who turns his coat.

entries.clue: Clothing accessory and linked merchandise worn by page (6)

indicatorNotes.worn by: something worn is carried round a body, so the merchandise letters wrap round P

blocks.note: a tie-in is merchandise linked to a film or show

annotation.surface: A page boy wearing an accessory and some branded goods.
annotation.walkthrough: The page wears the merchandise in the surface; in the wordplay it is the other way round, with P inside TIE-IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a small ornamental pin that holds a necktie in place is one kind of clothing accessory.

entries.clue: Engineers passionate about new industrial plant (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean around, so the letters for passionate go round N

annotation.surface: Engineers who are excited about a new factory.
annotation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps and a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a works that purifies crude oil or sugar is one kind of industrial plant.

entries.clue: Part of train perhaps drew near London’s West End (5)

indicatorNotes.West End: on a map west is on the left, and the left-hand end of a word written across is its first letter

blocks.note: the left-hand, opening letter of London

annotation.surface: A railway carriage pulling into London's theatre district.
annotation.walkthrough: The train is a caravan of animals, not a railway one; 'perhaps' flags that this is one member among others. The West End is London's theatre district, but here it is the end of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a desert caravan is called a train, and each animal in the line is one part of it.

entries.clue: Sharing out a couple of litres too much gin indiscriminately (9)

indicatorNotes.indiscriminately: done indiscriminately means done without care for order, so the letters of GIN are jumbled

annotation.surface: Pouring out far too much gin, a couple of litres, to anyone at all.
annotation.walkthrough: OTT, over the top, is informal British for excessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to apportion or distribute portions among people.

entries.clue: Former nurse unfortunately failed my loved ones and relatives (8,6)

indicatorNotes.unfortunately: unfortunately signals that things have gone wrong, so the letters of FAILED MY come out of order

annotation.surface: An ex-nurse confessing she let down the people closest to her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former nurse' reads as one retired person; nurse is really a verb here, meaning to look after.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the wider kin network of aunts, cousins and grandparents beyond parents and children.

entries.clue: Spies on army reserve chaps after short time (6,6)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the short time is written first and the rest follows it

blocks.note: TA = Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

annotation.surface: Spies keeping watch on reservist soldiers after a brief interval.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spies on' looks like a verb phrase; Spies is the noun definition and 'on' is RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: operatives who gather intelligence covertly for a government.

entries.clue: Side ultimately score five, being overcome by joy (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of score is taken
indicatorNotes.being overcome by: to be overcome is to be swamped, so the joy letters close over the pair

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five

annotation.surface: A sports team that nets five goals and is overwhelmed with joy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' reads as a team, and 'score five' as its result; Side is the definition and 'score' only supplies its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense from architecture: a drawing showing one face of a building, as in the front or side view.

entries.clue: One used to turn left by hospital before closure of route (5)

indicatorNotes.closure of: a closure is an ending, so the closing letter of route is taken

blocks.note: at = by, as in 'at the door'
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: Directions for a driver turning left by the hospital before a road closure.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all driving; the turning is done to wood or metal, and 'by' and 'before' do quiet work as AT and a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Turn in its woodworking sense, to shape on a spinning machine; this tool is the machine that does it.

entries.clue: Life is special, flag being twirled around (6)

indicatorNotes.being twirled: twirling spins a thing round, so the word for flag is turned back to front
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the turned word encloses SP

annotation.surface: A cheerful motto about life while someone waves a flag around.
annotation.walkthrough: The waving flag is a banner in the surface; here it is the verb, to weaken or tire.
annotation.definitionFit: Life in the sense of liveliness or vivacity; this French borrowing means spirit and sparkle.

entries.clue: Theatre set up marquee to host popular material (9)

indicatorNotes.set up: set up means raised, and in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards
indicatorNotes.to host: a host takes guests in, so the tent letters hold IN inside

blocks.note: a marquee is a large tent; split around IN

annotation.surface: A theatre company putting up a marquee to stage crowd-pleasing material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like the stuff being staged; it is the adjective, as in 'material to the case'.
annotation.definitionFit: Material as an adjective, meaning relevant or significant, as in material evidence.

entries.clue: Increasingly bad-tempered doctor swallowing drink that is initially relaxing (8)

indicatorNotes.swallowing: swallowing takes something inside, so the doctor's letters close round the drink
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of relaxing is taken

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner; split around RUM

annotation.surface: A crabby doctor who knocks back a drink meant to calm him down.
annotation.walkthrough: GP, a family doctor, is the standard crossword doctor.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: 'increasingly' supplies the -er, more cross or crabby than before.

entries.clue: Brother starts to experience yearning — head for something to eat (6,3)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their opening letters, so experience and yearning give one letter each

blocks.note: a monk is a religious brother
first letters of experience and yearning

annotation.surface: A friar feeling the first pangs of hunger and making for the dinner table.
annotation.walkthrough: A monkey nut is the British name for a peanut in its shell. 'Head for' reads as 'go towards'; head is NUT.
annotation.definitionFit: A vague definition by example: a peanut still in its shell is one thing among many you might eat.

entries.clue: Caught by short projectile, sure to capsize with fifty on board (5,3)

annotation.definitionNote: a phrase describing the thing: the dartboard centre worth fifty

indicatorNotes.Caught by: something caught is held, so the reversed word is held inside the shortened projectile
indicatorNotes.short: short means lacking, so the projectile loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to capsize: a capsized boat is upside down, and in a down clue the word for sure is turned to read upwards

blocks.note: BULLET without its T; split around SEY

annotation.surface: A boat hit by gunfire overturning with fifty people aboard.
annotation.walkthrough: The shipwreck scene makes 'on board' mean aboard a vessel; the board is a dartboard, and 'fifty' is the score, not a head count.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the inner red centre of a dartboard is the only target that scores fifty.

entries.clue: Border resident shot me with airgun (8)

indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is broken or ruined, so the letters of me and airgun fall into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters, joined to ME by 'with'

annotation.surface: Someone living near a frontier who has been hit with a pellet gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a national frontier; it is a flower border in a garden.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition by example: a common bedding plant that lives in a garden flower border.

entries.clue: Think about eating head of gingerbread man (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned round, as in about-turn, so THINK is written backwards
indicatorNotes.eating: eating takes something inside, so the turned word holds G
indicatorNotes.head of: the head is the top or front, so the first letter of gingerbread

blocks.note: used as printed; split around G once turned

annotation.surface: Musing on biting the head off a gingerbread man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gingerbread man' reads as one thing; man is the definition, a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword convention: the pieces in chess are called men, and this is the one that moves in an L shape.

entries.clue: Hot — heading towards 45 degrees with many keeling over (6)

indicatorNotes.keeling over: to keel over is to topple, so in a down clue the pair is tipped to read upwards

blocks.note: north-east is 45 degrees on a compass

annotation.surface: A heatwave with the thermometer approaching 45 and people collapsing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' and '45 degrees' paint a heatwave; the degrees are a compass bearing, and hot means taken illegally.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: hot goods have been taken by a thief and are risky to handle.

entries.clue: Cops seen in Ontario less regularly (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so the letters are taken at every other position

annotation.surface: Fewer police officers are spotted in Ontario these days.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cops' reads as police; it is the verb, as in 'cops it'. 'Less regularly' pretends to be a phrase about frequency.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for catching or arresting someone, as a detective finally pins down a suspect.

entries.clue: Consecutive notes in descending scale heard until now (2,3)

indicatorNotes.heard: heard means taken in by the ear, so the notes are said and their sound spells the entry

blocks.note: going down the sol-fa scale, soh comes straight before fah; in a non-rhotic accent fah sounds like far

annotation.surface: A music lesson: two neighbouring notes on the way down the scale.
annotation.walkthrough: The tonic sol-fa scale runs doh ray me fah soh lah te; coming down, soh is followed by fah.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: up to this point in time, as in 'nothing has gone wrong yet'.

entries.clue: Antisocial lout set fire to boat whose interior’s about to turn black (9)

indicatorNotes.whose interior’s: the interior is the inside, so the new letters are placed inside the boat word
indicatorNotes.to turn: turning round a word reverses it, so RE becomes ER

blocks.note: a tug is a boat; split around ERB

annotation.surface: A yob who torches a boat and watches its insides char black.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn black' reads as charring; 'about to turn' is RE reversed and black is just B.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: someone who drops rubbish in public spaces is one kind of antisocial lout.

entries.clue: Staff working to support sonar operator, perhaps? (5)

indicatorNotes.to support: a support holds something up from below, so in a down clue ON sits under BAT

blocks.note: bats find their way by echolocation, a natural sonar

annotation.surface: Staff on duty backing up the sonar operator on a submarine.
annotation.walkthrough: The sonar operator looks like a naval job; 'perhaps' marks it as a playful description of a bat.
annotation.definitionFit: Staff as a stick or rod, like one carried by a conductor, a relay runner or a police officer.

entries.clue: Problem with Duke’s meal (4,10)

blocks.note: a beef is a grievance, a problem
the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo

annotation.surface: The Duke has an issue with his dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts and the 's links wordplay to definition; the dish is fillet baked in pastry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a fillet of steak wrapped in pastry and baked is a classic dinner dish.

entries.clue: Swimmer last to get aboard cutter? (8)

indicatorNotes.last to: the last of a word is its final letter, so get gives its closing T
indicatorNotes.aboard: aboard means inside a vessel, so the letter goes inside the word for cutter

blocks.note: a surgeon cuts; split around T

annotation.surface: A swimmer climbing onto a small sailing boat.
annotation.walkthrough: A cutter is a small boat, which fits 'aboard'; the question mark says it is one who cuts, a surgeon.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large fish prized for caviar is one kind of swimmer.

entries.clue: Large vessel is in capital (5)

blocks.note: a big cask for wine or beer; three letters

annotation.surface: A big ship sitting in a capital's harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; a tun is a large cask for wine or beer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the chief city of Tunisia is one of the world's capitals.
